subject: Post-call: Performance & Concurrency requirements / Redwood quota negotiation
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: John Lee <john.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Mar 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — Performance targets, concurrency, and next steps

Hi John — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of what we heard (please correct me if I missed anything):
- Primary use case: near-real-time customer-facing feature that streams partial LLM responses to users (UI shows streaming tokens).
- Latency SLO: p95 generation latency target <= 250 ms for prompt sets of average length ~120 tokens; tail latency more important than median.
- Throughput: sustained ~1,200 requests/sec with peaks up to ~2,500 req/sec during business-critical windows.
- Concurrency: expected ~800 concurrent active requests (parallel streamed connections). Long-lived connections (websocket/HTTP streaming) are used; average completion time ~400 ms.
- Token/window limits: typical response length ~150 tokens; many requests are short but high QPS.

Questions we raised for you to confirm:
- Are all prod requests originating from a single region (us-west), or will we see cross-region traffic?
- Do you have connection pooling / keepalive on your side (recommended) or will clients open new connections per request?

Immediate next steps (action items):
1) I’ll share a draft quota/rate proposal from Redwood and a short SLO worksheet for you to validate expected concurrency/throughput distributions. (attached)
2) Please send any observed baseline metrics you have (current QPS, tail latencies, open connections) — even rough numbers are helpful.
3) If the numbers above are accurate, we’ll route this into our Dedicated quota approval & ramp plan; I’ll loop in Vivek to confirm burst/soft-limits and scheduling.

Attachment: SLO_worksheet.xlsx (xlsx, 42 KB)

Thanks — talk soon.
—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0187

On Sun, 29 Mar 2026 at 15:00 John Lee <john.lee@acme.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the call — looking forward to next steps.

From: John Lee <john.lee@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyanka Sharma <priyanka@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Performance targets, concurrency, and next steps

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Region: yes, initially US-West only (we’ll evaluate multi-region later).
- Baseline numbers (today, prototype): ~400 req/sec sustained, p95 ~350 ms (inference only), median ~120 ms.
- Peak plan: auto-scaling frontend can push bursts to ~2,200 req/sec for 3–5 minute windows during campaigns.
- Concurrency: Our product opens long-lived streaming connections; we typically see ~600 concurrent active streams in production tests, but expect growth to ~900 over 6 months.
- Connection behavior: we do use connection pooling and HTTP keep-alive on our side for most clients, but some third-party integrations will open new connections per request (we can add a proxy later).

Question: For p95 tail improvements, does Redwood recommend specific model variants / batching configuration for streaming workloads? Also, do you have hard rate limits (per-minute/per-second) that would affect short bursts?

We’re happy to review your worksheet and the proposal — Priyanka is our infra lead and will help validate numbers.

—John
Product Ops, Acme

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: John Lee <john.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood proposal + rate-limit/quota notes (draft)

John — thanks for the numbers, that helps a lot. Based on your baseline and expected growth, we put together a draft quota and operational plan. High level:

- Recommended reserved capacity: Dedicated pool sized for sustained 1,500 req/sec with headroom for 2.5x burst handling via autoscale (burst target ~3,750 req/sec for short windows).
- Connection/concurrency guidance:
  - Provision for 1,000 concurrent streaming connections (we recommend starting at 1,000 to avoid headroom surprises).
  - Use connection pooling + HTTP keepalive; prefer long-lived connections over new TCP/TLS handshakes per request to minimize tail latency.
  - If clients cannot pool, add an edge proxy to aggregate connections.
- Rate limits & quotas (default Redwood hosted limits):
  - Soft per-tenant QPS cap: 600 req/sec (enforced as a soft throttle for hosted).
  - Hard per-tenant token throughput: 1,000,000 tokens/minute (can be increased with Dedicated or custom contracts).
  - Concurrent connections default: 200 active streaming connections (can be raised on Dedicated).

Given your numbers, hosted defaults will be insufficient — we recommend Dedicated or a reserved quota with explicit increases to the soft caps. We’ve attached a short PDF proposal with the recommended commitment tiers and estimated monthly costs for the Dedicated pool aligned to your load profile.

Attachment: redwood_quota_proposal.pdf (pdf, 18 KB)

Operational notes & optimizations (quick wins):
- Use model variants with smaller context + dynamic quantization for short responses to reduce per-token compute and tail latency.
- Enable prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts to drop tail p95 by ~10–30% depending on reuse.
- Configure client-side connection pooling + keepalives; set idle keepalive to 60s and max connections per host to 200.
- For bursty traffic, implement short-term request queuing at the edge (e.g., 100 ms buffer) to allow better batching and reduce tokens/sec cost.

Next steps:
1) Vivek — can you confirm approval window for increasing concurrent connection quota to 1,000 for Acme and the burst allowance?
2) John/Priyanka — confirm you’re comfortable with Dedicated cost estimate; if yes, we’ll prepare a formal quote and standard SOW.
3) Marissa & Stephanie will sync with infra on any security/compliance checklist once Acme signs the LOI.

I’ve also shared our HubSpot deal link and the SLO worksheet for you to edit.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood proposal + rate-limit/quota notes (draft)

Looping in Rishi for finance/commit approvals. Quick decision notes: 

- Approve increasing concurrent streaming connections to 1,000 for Acme under Dedicated trial. We’ll provision a dedicated pool and add a temporary burst allowance of 3x baseline for the first 30 days.
- Legal/Proc: Marissa — please route the draft SOW and quote to Rishi; finance will need expected monthly commit and an outline of termination/overage terms.
- Stephanie — follow up with the infra docs for recommended client keepalive/pooling configs so the onboarding playbook is ready.

Marissa — go ahead and generate the formal quote and include a one-page appendix describing rate-limit behavior during bursts (soft throttles vs. hard limits) and the escalation path.

—Vivek
Head of Solutions
Redwood Inference
